subject: StrideCorp deployment matrix and action items
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@stridecorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call notes — deployment matrix & immediate asks

Hi Liam,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we heard on the call and the concrete asks so we can align engineering workstreams:

Pain points (as described):
- Unpredictable tail latency during morning/evening bursts; p99 spikes up to ~900ms today for ~512-token responses.
- Cost per successful session is high due to conservative batching and frequent KV cold starts.
- Need for predictable latency for customer-facing chat (SLOs) while preserving capacity for large offline scoring jobs.

Goals you shared:
- Target p95 < 100ms for 512-token interactive responses; p99 target <= 200–250ms during sustained load.
- Steady-state throughput ~250 qps with peaks ~850–950 qps.
- Support occasional 4k-token batch scoring runs (throughput-oriented, can tolerate higher latency).

Initial technical constraints we captured:
- Preferred deployment: private VPC or Redwood Dedicated in us-west-2 for GDPR-eu adjacent customers; fallback to Hosted for canary.
- Model footprint: currently running a 13B quantized model; considering 70B for highest quality but cost increases expected.
- KV cache TTL today is low (30s); this contributes to cold-start cost.

Suggested immediate next actions (we can start these in parallel):
1) Fill and return the attached SLA/infra questionnaire (Stride_SLA_Questionnaire.xlsx) — network egress, VPC peering, approved IP ranges.
2) Share traffic profile (per-minute qps histogram) and a sample session trace for three representative users.
3) For Redwood SRE: we will draft a short deployment matrix showing 3 options (Dedicated single-region, Dedicated multi-node sharded, Private VPC hybrid). See attached draft matrix (deployment_matrix_v1.xlsx).
4) Tentative canary window: we propose 10/04–10/08 for a limited traffic pilot (if network approvals are fast).

Technical assumptions we will validate:
- p99 targets assume continuous batching + KV prefix caching and an autoscaling policy tolerant of short CPU/GPU spin-up.
- For the interactive SLO, we recommend model quantization to INT8 or low-bit mixed precision and an H100-backed pool for steady-state.

Attachments: Stride_SLA_Questionnaire.xlsx, deployment_matrix_v1.xlsx, stride_network_vpc.png

Please confirm the traffic/profile numbers and whether your security team can share VPC peering details (or if you prefer a private package deployment).

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@stridecorp.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call notes — deployment matrix & immediate asks

Liam, Irene —

Thanks for the context. A few items from the infra/serving perspective and the proposed deployment matrix we discussed:

1) Deployment options (matrix summary)
  - Option A: Dedicated single-region H100 pool (best p99 latency, higher cost). Good for strict interactive SLOs.
  - Option B: Dedicated multi-node (sharded) with mixed GPU types and autoscale for bursts (balanced cost/latency).
  - Option C: Private VPC (customer-managed infra) — best for data isolation, requires VPC peering and slightly longer onboarding.

2) Model & runtime recommendations
  - Interactive: quantized 13B–30B model on H100 with 1–2 concurrent streams per GPU for low latency; INT8 quantization preferred.
  - Quality-sensitive fallback: we recommend a 70B model variant for a small subset of requests with an automatic routing policy (only used when quality delta is required).

3) Autoscaling & batching heuristics
  - Burst handling: use continuous batching with 10–20ms batching window and a dynamic concurrency cap to avoid p99 amplification.
  - Cache sizing: increase hot-prefix TTL to 3–5 minutes for conversational workloads; approximate memory impact: +8–12GB per 100k active prefixes.

4) Metrics we need from you to size pools accurately
  - Per-minute qps histogram for the last 30 days (sample upload link would suffice).
  - Representative traces showing sequence length distribution and cold-start frequency.
  - Any enforced egress limits or IP allowlists for canary endpoints.

Next steps I propose:
- Irene & Marissa to coordinate a Thursday 11am PT run-through with your infra lead (Trevor).
- You (Liam) return the completed SLA questionnaire (EOD Wed).
- I will prepare a more detailed deployment matrix (node counts, estimated costs, and p99 projections) and share by Friday.

Also including a short checklist of items our SRE will need for a private/VPC pilot in the attachment.

Regards,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
